issues.message: The plan name parsed from `<!-- mb-plan:... -->` is joined directly to `plans_dir`; absolute paths, `..` components, and symlinks can make `_titles` read files outside the Memory Bank.
issues.fix: Reject non-basename marker values and resolve each candidate through a canonical-under-plans-dir check before reading it.

issues.message: Archive confirmation checks only the generated heading. Two legacy sections with the same heading, or a plan reopened and closed again on the same day, reuse that heading; the later block is then dropped without its body being appended, violating the no-deletion invariant.
issues.fix: Use a collision-resistant archive identity and verify the complete archived block before adding its drop key.

issues.message: The append-before-remove guard verifies only that an archive heading exists. After a partial prior run, a fail-safe no-write from the append helper can be mistaken for success because the old heading remains, causing the current section body to be removed without confirmation; successful retries also duplicate already-appended blocks.
issues.fix: Skip only when the complete exact block is already present, and verify that exact block after every append before rewriting status.md.

issues.message: `--keep N` retains the first N dated sections in file order, not the newest N by date as required. An out-of-order status.md archives newer state while retaining older state.
issues.fix: Parse heading dates, select the newest N dated sections by date, and preserve original order when rendering survivors.

issues.message: Mixed v1/v2 merging preserves the done bit but always replaces an earlier non-empty stage name with the later name. A richer v1 item such as a closeout detail is therefore silently lost when a shorter duplicate v2 stage follows it, contradicting the stated information-retention invariant.
issues.fix: Resolve duplicate stage names without discarding distinct text, preserving richer content explicitly in the rendered block or archive.

issues.message: The cap resolver accepts `0`, while `cmd_apply` treats a non-positive cap as disabled. `MB_CHECKLIST_MAX_LINES=0` or `checklist_max_lines=0` therefore bypasses the documented hard cap instead of falling back or reporting invalid configuration.
issues.fix: Require a strictly positive integer and fall back to 100 or fail validation when the configured cap is zero.
